note: Gin Type Tray is a presentation-only bridge that restyles the Type Tray /node/add screen for the Gin admin theme. It has no config, permissions, schema, entities, or Drush (configure=null). Its only live-inspectable, module-owned effect is that its route subscriber (GinTypeTrayRouteSubscriber) overrides the node.add_page route's _controller to \Drupal\gin_type_tray\Controller\GinTypeTrayController::addPage; the rest is theme-hook/template overrides (type_tray_teaser, type_tray_page), a CSS library swap (css/gin_type_tray.css), and icon preprocessing. Because the module has no buildable config of its own, the hard case is grounded in the Type Tray screen it themes: the agent configures a content type to appear in that tray via type_tray node-type third-party settings (type_tray.type_category), verified live. The medium case reads the live node.add_page controller to prove the route override is active.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal gin_type_tray module do, and what two things does it require to be present to work?
evals.expected_output: It restyles the Type Tray module's /node/add content-creation screen to match the Gin administrative theme, including dark-mode support. It requires the type_tray module and the gin theme (its composer.json requires drupal/type_tray and drupal/gin). It has no configuration of its own.

evals.prompt: How does gin_type_tray change the Drupal /node/add page without patching the Type Tray module? Name the route it overrides and roughly how the styling is applied.
evals.expected_output: A route subscriber (GinTypeTrayRouteSubscriber) overrides the node.add_page route's _controller to GinTypeTrayController::addPage (a subclass of Type Tray's controller that swaps the default icon). Styling comes from hook_theme_registry_alter() repointing the type_tray_teaser/type_tray_page theme hooks at this module's Twig templates, plus hook_library_info_alter() swapping in css/gin_type_tray.css, and hook_preprocess_type_tray_teaser() inlining SVG icons for dark mode.

evals.prompt: Where do I configure gin_type_tray itself, and where do the content-type categories and icons shown in the tray actually come from?
evals.expected_output: gin_type_tray has no configuration page (configure=null) and no settings of its own - enabling it (with Gin active) is the whole setup. The categories, icons, thumbnails and descriptions come from the parent Type Tray module's per-content-type third-party settings (node.type.*.third_party.type_tray, e.g. type_category, type_icon), configured on each content type's edit form; gin_type_tray only themes that output.

evals.prompt: On this running Drupal site, gin_type_tray is enabled. Inspect the live routing and state which controller method now handles the node.add_page route.
evals.expected_output: node.add_page is served by \Drupal\gin_type_tray\Controller\GinTypeTrayController::addPage, because gin_type_tray's route subscriber overrides the route's _controller default.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (which uses the Gin-themed Type Tray via gin_type_tray), create a content type with machine name 'gtt_task' and configure it so it appears grouped under a category on the Type Tray /node/add screen. Apply the change live.
evals.expected_output: A node type 'gtt_task' exists and carries a non-empty type_tray.type_category third-party setting so Type Tray (rendered by gin_type_tray) groups it under that category, e.g. $type->setThirdPartySetting('type_tray','type_category','gtt_marketing')->save().
